root_idea.summary: The root centers on distance and inclination: going far from a point or departing from a proper line.
root_idea.development: The notion of distance develops into exceeding due bounds, extravagance, and injustice through deviation from what is right; it also extends to physical sides, separation, and stature.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Form IV dictionary citation form.
Displayed as the Quranic nominal headword شَطَطٌ.

senses.definition: To depart from what is right; to exceed due bounds or act unjustly, especially in judgment.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic prohibitive construction وَلَا تُشْطِطْ, it means not to go beyond right conduct or deal unjustly in judging.

senses.definition: An excessive departure from truth or right; an extravagant or far-from-truth statement or claim.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrences, it describes a saying or claim that is excessively remote from the truth, including an assertion made about God.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become distant, remote, or far away; to pass beyond or away from a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a dwelling, place, or other location, and of moving far from a place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go beyond due bounds in bargaining, pricing, or demanding a price; also to go to great lengths in pursuing someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with commercial transactions, demands, and pursuit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To distress or afflict someone and treat that person unjustly, wrongfully, injuriously, or tyrannically.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use describing harmful unjust treatment of another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be rough, harsh, or coarse in speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the manner or quality of speaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exert oneself or persist in exceeding due bounds and acting unjustly or wrongfully.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II conveys strenuous or sustained engagement in the excessive or unjust action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie with another in exceeding bounds or acting unjustly, and to surpass or overcome that person in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal construction involving competition in the excessive or unjust conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bank or side of a river or valley; for a valley, the rising ground beside its bottom.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical noun for the side or bank adjoining a watercourse or valley.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The side or half of a camel’s hump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical use referring to either side of the hump.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An extravagant or exorbitant action or affair that exceeds due bounds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of conduct or an affair, as distinct from the Quranic use describing an extravagant saying or claim.
A nominal expression for the distance of a space or route.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The distance between a person’s extremities; hence tallness, beauty of stature, or well-proportioned stature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical description of extended or well-proportioned bodily stature.
A concrete noun, also reported in a plural form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel with a large hump, or one large on the two sides of its hump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a camel’s hump.
The identification is reported as having no established authority.
An adjectival use applied to anything characterized by remoteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person of tall or well-proportioned stature, whose extremities are far apart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical description of stature; the source illustrates it with both male and female persons.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unjust, wrongful, injurious, or tyrannical in judging.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of unjust conduct in judgment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Difficulty, distress, affliction, trouble, or inconvenience.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived noun for hardship or troubling circumstances.

cautions: The public verb headword is normalized to the Form IV perfect أَشْطَطَ; the supplied Quran occurrence is its imperfect prohibitive form تُشْطِطْ.
The bird meaning شَطْشَاطٌ is retained because it is a reported lexical item, but its source explicitly marks the identification as lacking established authority.
